question.content:
A company can use its current resources to produce hats and boots as shown in this production possibilities curve (PPC).

[[☃ image 1]]

**Which of the following represents a movement from inefficiency to efficiency in this PPC?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A line graph depicts a production possibilities curve labeled P P C 1, representing the trade-off between the production of hats and an unspecified second good. The graph has a vertical axis labeled Hats and a horizontal axis labeled Quantity. The curve P P C 1 is downward-sloping and concave, starting at point V at (0, 8) on the Y-axis and ending at point R at (9, 0) on the X-axis. Points are marked along and within the curve. Five points are marked on the graph. Point V is at (0, 8) on the P P C 1 curve. Point R is at (10, 0) on the P P C 1 curve. Point S is at approximately (7, 5) on the P P C 1 curve. Point T is at approximately (5, 3) inside the P P C 1 curve. Point U is at approximately (9, 6) outside the P P C 1 curve.

choices.clue: A movement from T to S represents a move from an inefficient combination of production to an efficient combination of production. S is efficient because it is *on* the PPC and T is inefficient because it is *inside* the PPC.
If you chose this option, you might think that R is inefficient because it is on an axis. However, R is efficient because it is on the PPC and any point on the PPC is efficient.
If you chose this option, you might think V is inefficient because it is on an axis. However, V is efficient because it is on the PPC and any point on the PPC is efficient.

A movement from S to U represents a change from an attainable combination of production to an unattainable combination of production. S is attainable and efficient because it is *on* the PPC. U is unattainable because it is outside the PPC.
V is an attainable combination because it is on the PPC, but T is inside the PPC, so it cannot be efficient.
